logline: After a financial scandal wipes out her savings, idealist attorney Diane Lockhart joins a Black-owned Chicago law firm and finds herself navigating a fractured political America - The Good Wife's sharper, angrier spinoff.

renewal.note: Six seasons aired on Paramount+ (formerly CBS All Access) from 2017 to 2022. The show concluded with Season 6 in November 2022.

bollymeter.basis: 98% Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic 80 for Season 1; critics praised Christine Baranski's commanding performance and the show's sharper political edge over its predecessor.

pull_quotes.text: The spinoff feels appropriately like an extension on the brand, with appeal for those who followed The Good Wife.

seasons.review_body: The Good Fight launched on CBS All Access in February 2017 - the same week as the first presidential travel ban - and critics immediately noted that its timing gave it an almost journalistic charge. The season earned 98% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic of 80. Christine Baranski's Diane Lockhart anchors everything: her financial ruin and forced reinvention at Reddick, Boseman and Kolstad gave the show an entry point that felt more urgent than anything in The Good Wife. Cush Jumbo and Rose Leslie were praised for holding their own opposite Baranski. Critics divided only on whether the pilot burned through setup too quickly - the consensus was that by episode three, it had fully found its footing.

episode_reviews.title: Inauguration
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Diane Lockhart loses everything - savings, firm, reputation - in a single episode and must start over. A propulsive setup that uses the political moment as economic vertigo for its protagonist.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Diane watching the inauguration on television as her world collapses simultaneously - the show's thesis stated in images rather than dialogue.

bollymeter.basis: 96% Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic 70 for Season 2; critics remained positive while noting the expanded episode count occasionally led to pacing issues.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 (March 2018) expanded to thirteen episodes and maintained a 96% Rotten Tomatoes score, though the Metacritic slipped to 70 - a reflection of some critics feeling the additional length diluted momentum. The season pushed deeper into its police brutality and political satire threads, with Delroy Lindo's Adrian Boseman given more space. The Good Fight's willingness to structure episodes as formal experiments - a musical episode, a "what if" alternate history installment - began here and divided audiences, though critics largely applauded the ambition. Audra McDonald joined the cast and drew strong notices. The season is the show's longest and most uneven, but its highs match Season 1.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 is broader and more formally experimental than Season 1 - the ambition is evident, but thirteen episodes stretch the material slightly thin.

bollymeter.basis: 96% Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic 83; The Guardian wrote that Season 3 'has now become fully its own thing' - the show's creative confidence at its peak.

pull_quotes.text: The series has now become fully its own thing while resisting simple classification through its experimental storytelling approaches.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 (March-May 2019) returned to ten episodes and scored 96% on Rotten Tomatoes with a Metacritic of 83 - the show's joint-best Metacritic score. Critics declared the show fully emancipated from its Good Wife origins. The Guardian noted it had escaped easy categorization. The season deepened the show's satirical portrait of legal practice under political chaos, introduced animated sequences to comment on censorship, and gave Diane Lockhart a psychedelic subplot that split critics but impressed those who embraced the formal risks. Delroy Lindo's expanded role was universally praised. By Season 3, the show had established itself as the smartest legal drama on any platform.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 3 is The Good Fight fully realized - leaner than Season 2 and more formally daring, with Baranski and Lindo at the height of their chemistry.

bollymeter.basis: 95% Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic 84; COVID-19 cut the season short at 7 episodes, but critics noted the compressed run felt tight and purposeful.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 aired April-May 2020 and was cut short at seven episodes due to COVID-19 production shutdowns. It scored 95% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic of 84 - paradoxically the strongest Metacritic rating the show had achieved. Critics suggested the enforced brevity tightened a show that had occasionally sprawled. The season tracked the first year of the Trump administration's Chicago legal fallout with characteristic acidity. The abrupt finale drew mixed feelings - the season's ending was provisional rather than resolved - but the compact run also kept the energy high from start to finish.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 4 is the shortest run and, in some ways, the most controlled - COVID-curtailed but sharper for it.

bollymeter.basis: 91% Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic 80; IndieWire noted Season 5 retained 'all the hallmarks of the wild Good Fight imagination with an even greater sense of confidence.'

pull_quotes.text: All the hallmarks of the wild Good Fight imagination persist with an even greater sense of confidence.

seasons.review_body: Season 5 (June-August 2021) scored 91% on Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic 80. Following the departure of Cush Jumbo, the season restructured around Baranski, Lindo, and new addition Charmaine Bingwa. Critics noted the transition was handled with care and that the show's satirical energy - covering January 6 fallout, corporate law culture, and racial politics in Chicago - remained as sharp as ever. IndieWire praised the season's confidence. The series was renewed for a sixth and final season shortly after, signaling the network's satisfaction with the critical reception even as the Tomatometer dipped below earlier peaks.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 5 absorbs Cush Jumbo's departure better than feared - the new cast additions land, and the satirical energy holds.

bollymeter.basis: 94% Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic 75 for the final season; critics praised the farewell for giving its characters honest endings, even as some felt the show had run out of new legal terrain to satirize.

seasons.review_body: The sixth and final season of The Good Fight (September-November 2022) scored 94% on Rotten Tomatoes with a Metacritic of 75 - slightly below the show's mid-run peak but still firmly in the positive consensus. Critics credited the Kings with providing Diane Lockhart a conclusion that felt earned rather than sentimental. The season tackled its most explicitly political material - election denialism, Big Law ethics, the ongoing culture wars - without losing the legal-procedural infrastructure that held the show together. Christine Baranski's final scene generated particular critical attention. As send-offs go, the consensus was that The Good Fight said what it came to say.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 6 gives the show a proper ending - Baranski exits on her own terms, and the political satire lands its final punches.
